title: Chromatin and gene-regulatory dynamics of the developing human cerebral cortex at single-cell resolution.
authors: Trevino, Alexandro E; Muller, Fabian; Andersen, Jimena; Sundaram, Laksshman; Kathiria, Arwa; Shcherbina, Anna; Farh, Kyle; Chang, Howard Y; Pasca, Anca M; Kundaje, Anshul; Pasca, Sergiu P; Greenleaf, William J
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过单细胞转录组与染色质可及性图谱解析人类大脑皮层发育中的基因调控动态，并利用神经网络模型预测非编码突变对TF结合位点的破坏，虽涉及TF-DNA调控但以基因组学为主，缺乏三维互作建模与机制研究。
abstract: Genetic perturbations of cortical development can lead to neurodevelopmental disease, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD). To identify genomic regions crucial to corticogenesis, we mapped the activity of gene-regulatory elements generating a single-cell atlas of gene expression and chromatin accessibility both independently and jointly. This revealed waves of gene regulation by key transcription factors (TFs) across a nearly continuous differentiation trajectory, distinguished the expression programs of glial lineages, and identified lineage-determining TFs that exhibited strong correlation between linked gene-regulatory elements and expression levels. These highly connected genes adopted an active chromatin state in early differentiating cells, consistent with lineage commitment. Base-pair-resolution neural network models identified strong cell-type-specific enrichment of noncoding mutations predicted to be disruptive in a cohort of ASD individuals and identified frequently disrupted TF binding sites. This approach illustrates how cell-type-specific mapping can provide insights into the programs governing human development and disease.
abstract_zh: 皮层发育的遗传扰动可导致神经发育疾病，包括自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）。为了识别对皮层形成至关重要的基因组区域，我们绘制了基因调控元件的活性图谱，生成了基因表达和染色质可及性的单细胞图谱，既独立又联合分析。这揭示了关键转录因子（TFs）在近乎连续的分化轨迹上的基因调控波，区分了胶质谱系的表达程序，并识别出在连锁基因调控元件与表达水平之间表现出强相关性的谱系决定转录因子。这些高度连接的基因在早期分化细胞中呈现活跃的染色质状态，与谱系承诺一致。碱基对分辨率的神经网络模型识别出在ASD个体队列中预测具有破坏性的非编码突变的强细胞类型特异性富集，并识别出频繁被破坏的转录因子结合位点。该方法展示了细胞类型特异性图谱如何为理解人类发育和疾病调控程序提供见解。
